title: A licensing control can contract early critical-mineral shipments and raise price uncertainty without proving durable geopolitical leverage
source_unit: China export-control announcement, MOFCOM licensing update, and USITC March 2024 critical-mineral briefing
geography: China and international gallium/germanium supply chain with U.S. import exposure

observations.period: July 3-August 1, 2023 through December 13, 2023; export-control implementation, early shipment contraction, and price response

denominator.unit: specified covered gallium and germanium items; shipment and price comparisons are monthly or cited-date comparisons, not a complete market census

licensing_gate.value: Covered gallium and germanium items required export permission and supporting end-user, end-use, technical, contract, and importer information beginning August 1, 2023

approved_applications.value: MOFCOM reported on November 30, 2023 that some applications had been approved and some companies had obtained dual-use export licences

wrought_exports.value: USITC reported Chinese wrought gallium exports of 6,876 kg in July, zero in August and September, and 227 kg in October; germanium exports fell from 7,965 kg in July to zero in August, 1 kg in September, and 590 kg in October

price_response.value: USITC reported October gallium at 1,975 yuan/kg, 18% above July, global gallium prices up 68% since July, and germanium prices up 21% from January 1 by December 13

downstream_effect.unit: missing application-level approvals, destination shipments, inventories, qualified substitutes, firm redesign, production, employment, consumer prices, and bargaining concessions

mechanism.value: A licensing control can shift documentation, waiting, inventory, qualification, and price risk toward exporters and downstream buyers while producing visible early trade contraction without establishing a sustained cutoff or realized geopolitical concession

observations.method: Structured extraction from official Chinese export-control and MOFCOM statements and the USITC executive briefing; licensing, trade, price, and downstream-effect stages are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: Shipment and price figures are reported secondary data and do not isolate export-control causality from demand, inventories, market conditions, or other policy effects. No complete product, destination, application, firm, or household census is retained.
observations.subgroup: Covered gallium and germanium products, exporters, downstream semiconductor and technology applications, and U.S. import exposure; firm-level and worker-level outcomes are not identified.
observations.counterinterpretation: Approved licences, U.S. germanium stockpile and recovery activity, alternative suppliers, inventories, and application-specific substitution could buffer particular users; early contraction and price increases do not prove sustained shortage or leverage.

boundary: This record establishes a dated export-control, early shipment-contraction, and price-response sequence. It does not establish a sustained cutoff, U.S. shortage, firm-level production loss, household effect, or realized geopolitical concession.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from official Chinese policy statements and the USITC briefing; confidential contracts, firm files, personal data, and raw shipment microdata are not retained.
